rules.title: Prohibition on selling or providing coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process that generates or presents a report, study, or presentation publishing rental data in an aggregated and anonymous manner and does not recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates, or other rental contract terms for future leases. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product used for establishing rent or income limits in accordance with affordable housing guidelines of a local government, state, federal government, or other political subdivision. [§ 13.63.020(A)]; The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process, or provision or use of information, for conducting market research for project financing, conducting an appraisal, or conducting software research, testing, or training where competitor data is not used as an input in model operation at recommendation time. [§ 13.63.020(A)]
rules.quoted_span:
A. It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each month that a violation continues and each unit for which the algorithm was used constitutes a separate violation.
rules.exemptions: The restriction on coordinated pricing algorithms does not apply to a product or process that generates or presents a report, study, or presentation publishing rental data in an aggregated and anonymous manner and does not recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates, or other rental contract terms for future leases. [§ 13.63.020(A)]
rules.quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: City Attorney civil enforcement and penalties
rules.requirement: The City Attorney may bring a civil action for algorithmic rent setting violations seeking damages, injunctive relief, restitution or return of illegal profits, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with mandatory reasonable attorney's fees and costs awarded if the City Attorney prevails.

and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. The court shall award reasonable 
attorney’s fees and costs to the City Attorney if the City Attorney is the prevailing party 
in such a civil action.

rules.title: Requirement of Just Cause to Terminate Tenancy
rules.requirement: An owner shall not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice to terminate after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months. If additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months of occupancy, just cause applies only if all tenants have occupied for at least 12 months or at least one tenant has occupied for at least 24 months.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months, or, if additional adult tenants were added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, once all tenants have occupied for 12+ months or at least one tenant has occupied for 24+ months.

[§ 1946.2(e)(1); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in a nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, licensed residential care facility for the elderly, or adult residential facility are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(2); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(3); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in which the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains their principal residence at the residential real property are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(4); document-wide]; Single-family owner-occupied residences in which the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms (including an ADU or junior ADU), or a mobilehome, are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(5); document-wide]; A duplex in which the owner occupied one of the units as their principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues occupancy (where neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU) is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(6); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless the housing is a mobilehome) is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(7); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential real property (including a mobilehome) is exempt from this section if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, corporate-member LLC, or mobilehome park management, and the tenant has been provided the required statutory written exemption disclosure notice. (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy. (1) All of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the residential real property for 12 months or more.
(2) One or more tenants have continuously and lawfully
occupied the residential real property for 24 months or more.

If the intended occupant fails to move in within 90 days or occupy the unit for 12 consecutive months, the owner must offer the unit back to the displaced tenant at the same rent and lease terms in effect when the tenant vacated and reimburse reasonable moving expenses exceeding relocation assistance already paid, unless the occupant dies before completing 12 months of occupancy.

rules.title: Initial Inspection Notice and Scheduling Requirements
rules.requirement: Upon notice to terminate or before lease end, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of their right to request and attend an initial inspection, must conduct it no earlier than two weeks before move-out if requested, must provide at least 48 hours' written notice of inspection date and time (unless waived), and must include the statutory notice regarding abandoned property.

rules.quoted_span:

The purpose of the initial inspection shall be to allow the tenant an opportunity to remedy identified deficiencies, in a manner consistent with the rights and obligations of the parties under the rental agreement, in order to avoid deductions from the security. If a tenant chooses not to request an initial inspection, the duties of the landlord under this subdivision are discharged. If an inspection is requested, the parties shall attempt to schedule the inspection at a mutually acceptable date and time. agreed upon, or if a mutually agreed time cannot be scheduled but the tenant still wishes an inspection. The tenant and landlord may agree to forgo the 48-hour prior written notice by both signing a written waiver. “State law permits former tenants to reclaim abandoned personal property left at the former address of the tenant, subject to certain conditions. You may or may not be able to reclaim property without incurring additional costs, depending on the cost of storing the property and the length of time before it is reclaimed. In general, these costs will be lower the sooner you contact your former landlord after
being notified that property belonging to you was left behind after you moved out.”

rules.requirement: Upon terminating their interest in the premises, the landlord must either transfer the remaining security to their successor and give detailed written notice to the tenant, or return the remaining deposit to the tenant with an accounting.

rules.requirement: Security includes any payment, fee, deposit, or charge (except application screening fees under Section 1950.6) imposed at the start of tenancy to reimburse tenant-processing costs or as advance rent, and encompasses amounts used for rent default, repair of tenant-caused damages beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to restore inception cleanliness, or restoring or returning personal property if authorized by the lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: The cleaning standard in paragraph (3) applies only to tenancies for which the tenant's right to occupy begins after January 1, 2003.; Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant. [§ 1950.5(a); document-wide]
rules.exemptions: Application screening fees as provided in Section 1950.6.
rules.quoted_span:
(b) As used in this section, “security” means any payment, fee, deposit, or charge, including, but not limited to, any payment, fee, deposit, or charge, except as provided in Section 1950.6, that is imposed at the beginning of the tenancy to be used to reimburse the landlord for costs associated with processing a new tenant or that is imposed as an advance payment of rent, used or to be used for any purpose, including, but not limited to, any of the following:
(1) The compensation of a landlord for a
tenant’s default in the payment of rent.
(2) The repair of damages to the premises, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear, caused by the tenant or by a guest or licensee of the tenant.
(3) The cleaning of the premises upon termination of the tenancy necessary to return the unit to the same level of cleanliness it was in at the inception of the tenancy. The amendments to this paragraph enacted by the act adding this sentence shall apply only to tenancies for which the tenant’s right to occupy begins after January 1, 2003.
(4) To remedy future defaults by the tenant in any obligation under the rental agreement to restore, replace, or return personal property or appurtenances, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear, if the
security deposit is authorized to be applied thereto by the rental agreement.

rules.title: Deductions for Uncured Deficiencies Itemized in Inspection Statement
rules.requirement: A landlord is permitted to use the security deposit for deductions itemized in the initial inspection statement that were not cured by the tenant, provided the deductions are for damages authorized by Section 1950.5.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant. [§ 1950.5(a); document-wide]
rules.exemptions: The initial inspection requirements of subdivision (f) do not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to subdivision (2), (3), or (4) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure. [§ 1950.5(f)(7)]
rules.quoted_span:
(5) Nothing in this subdivision shall prevent a landlord from using the security for deductions itemized in the statement provided for in paragraph (2) that were not cured by the tenant so long as the deductions are for damages authorized by

rules.title: Deductions for Post-Inspection or Hidden Deficiencies
rules.requirement: A landlord is permitted to use the security deposit for any authorized purpose specified in subdivision (b)(1) to (4) that occurs between the initial inspection and the return of possession, or that was not identified during the inspection due to the presence of tenant possessions.

rules.title: Mailing Address for Accounting and Security Deposit Mailings
rules.requirement: Any mailings to the tenant under subdivision (h) must be sent to the address provided by the tenant, or to the vacated unit if the tenant has not provided an address.

rules.title: Successor in Interest Rights and Duties for Transferred Security
rules.requirement: Upon receiving any portion of the security deposit transferred pursuant to subdivision (i)(1), the landlord's successor in interest assumes all rights and obligations of a landlord holding the security.

rules.title: Application screening fee authorization and scope
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee to cover the costs of obtaining information about the applicant (such as personal reference checks and consumer credit reports). A landlord or their agent may, but is not required to, accept and rely upon a consumer credit report presented by the applicant.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5. Under subdivision (l), this section is not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding Section 1950.5, when a landlord or their agent receives a request to rent a residential property from an applicant, the landlord or their agent may charge, pursuant to subdivision (c), that applicant an application screening fee to cover the costs of obtaining information about the applicant. The information requested and obtained by the landlord or their agent may include, but is not limited to, personal reference checks and consumer credit reports produced by consumer credit reporting agencies as defined in Section 1785.3. A landlord or their agent may, but is not required to, accept and rely upon a consumer credit report presented by an applicant.

rules.title: Maximum application screening fee and CPI adjustments
rules.requirement: The application screening fee charged cannot exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket costs and the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. In no case may the fee exceed thirty dollars ($30) per applicant, which may be adjusted annually commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant (adjustable annually based on CPI increases since January 1, 1998)
rules.interaction: Under subdivision (l), this section does not preempt provisions or regulations governing the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span:
(b) The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual
out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Prohibition on fee when rental unit unavailable
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Mandatory screening process prerequisites for charging fee
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may charge an application screening fee only if, at the time the fee is collected, they offer either: (A) a process where screening criteria are provided in writing with the application form, completed applications are considered in the order received, the first applicant meeting established criteria is approved, and applicants are not charged unless or until their application is actually considered (with inadvertent concurrent collections refunded within seven days); or (B) a process where the landlord returns the entire screening fee to any unselected applicant within 7 days of selecting a tenant or within 30 days of application submission, whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: refund within 7 days of unconsidered inadvertent collection; or full refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission
rules.exemptions: Under process option (A), the landlord is not required to refund a screening fee to an applicant denied after consideration for failing to meet established screening criteria, and may offer to apply the fee to another rental unit at the applicant's discretion instead of refunding.
rules.quoted_span:
(2) A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:
(A) An application screening process that complies with all of the following:
(i) Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received. The landlord’s screening criteria shall be provided to the applicant in writing together with the application form.
(ii) The first applicant who meets the landlord’s established screening criteria is approved for tenancy.
(iii) Applicants are not
charged an application screening fee unless or until their application is actually considered.
(iv) Clause (iii) shall not be considered violated if a landlord or their agent inadvertently collects an application screening fee from an applicant as the result of multiple concurrent application submissions, provided that the landlord or their agent issues a refund of the application screening fee within seven days to any applicant whose application is not considered. The landlord may offer, as an alternative to refunding the screening fee, the option, at the applicant’s discretion, for the screening fee paid by the applicant to be applied to an application for another rental unit offered by the landlord. A landlord or their agent shall not be required to refund an application screening fee to an applicant whose application is denied, after consideration, because the applicant does not meet the landlord’s established screening criteria.
(B) An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.

rules.title: Itemized receipt requirement for screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord or their agent must provide the applicant, personally or by mail, with a receipt for the screening fee paid that itemizes out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing information. The parties may agree to have the copy of the receipt delivered to an email account provided by the applicant.

rules.title: Refund of unused screening fee portion
rules.requirement: If the landlord or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any portion of the screening fee not used for purposes authorized by this section.

rules.title: Delivery of consumer credit report copy
rules.requirement: If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the landlord or their agent must provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving the report.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination and harassment by housing owners
rules.requirement: An owner of any housing accommodation is prohibited from discriminating against or harassing any person on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information.

rules.title: Prohibition on inquiries regarding protected classes of rental applicants
rules.requirement: An owner of any housing accommodation is prohibited from making or causing to be made any written or oral inquiry concerning the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of any person seeking to purchase, rent, or lease any housing accommodation.

rules.title: Prohibition on denying a dwelling based on discrimination
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to otherwise make unavailable or deny a dwelling based on discrimination because of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, familial status, source of income, disability, genetic information, veteran or military status, or national origin.

rules.title: Equal aggregation of co-residents' income in rental standards
rules.requirement: In the rental of housing, it is unlawful to use a financial or income standard that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons residing or proposing to reside together.

rules.title: Income eligibility standard restricted to tenant portion for subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: When assessing eligibility for the rental of housing where a government rent subsidy exists, a housing provider is prohibited from using a financial or income standard that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: Alternative evidence option required when using credit history for subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: A housing provider cannot use an applicant's credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant's discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of reasonable ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent, including government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
rules.exemptions: Subdivision (o) does not limit the ability of the owner of a housing accommodation to request information or documentation to verify employment, to request landlord references, or to verify the identity of a person. [Gov. Code § 12955(o)(2)]

rules.title: Duties when subsidized applicant provides alternative ability-to-pay evidence

To terminate tenancy for the purpose of demolition of a Protected Unit1, a landlord must: 
1. File with LAHD a Declaration of Intent to Evict for units regulated by the JCO per the Los Angeles
Municipal Code (LAMC) Section 165.03.I(1) or file with LAHD a  Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units
From Rental Housing Use for units regulated by the RSO.  Only RSO units are subject to the Ellis
Act provisions (LAMC 151.22-151.28).  All RSO units are Protected Units.
2. Serve tenants with a written notice to move out and file a copy of it with LAHD within 3 business
days online at https://lahd.service-now.com/efs. For more information go to
housing.lacity.gov/eviction-notices
3. Pay relocation assistance to tenants in compliance with the State law’s Housing Crisis Act
(California Government Code Section 66300 et seq.) or the City laws, whichever is higher.  City
laws require all tenants be paid relocation assistance in the amounts required by the RSO or JCO
within 15 days of serving a notice to terminate tenancy, which must be enhanced for lower income
tenants if the project is subject to the Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO), effective 2/11/2025
under Ordinances # 188481 and #188482.  The RSO and JCO amounts must also be enhanced for
lower income tenants under the HCA regardless of the RPO applicability.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination based on public assistance or housing subsidies
rules.requirement: A person furnishing rental accommodations, credit, or services cannot discriminate against any individual because they receive federal, state, or local public assistance or housing subsidies (including rental assistance or rental supplements), or because of any requirement of the public assistance or housing subsidy program.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person furnishing credit, services, or rental accommodations.
rules.quoted_span: 10. For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: Notice to quit and right to cure for nonpayment under written lease
rules.requirement: Upon neglect or refusal to pay rent due under a written lease, a landlord's fourteen days' notice to quit given in writing to the tenant is sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant pays or tenders all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in an action to recover possession.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease.
rules.exemptions: The lease is not determined if the tenant pays or tenders to the landlord or the landlord's attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

rules.title: Court continuance and cure protection for delayed government payments
rules.requirement: If nonpayment of rent was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth, or any municipality (or agency thereof) in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check, or voucher other than salary, the court must continue the hearing for not less than seven days to notify the agency and must treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent due with interest and costs of suit is tendered within that time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when neglect or refusal to pay rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth, or any municipality (or department, agency, or authority thereof) in mailing or delivering any subsistence or rental payment, check, or voucher other than a salary payment to the tenant or landlord.
rules.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any such action shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.

rules.title: Notice Required to Determine Estate at Will
rules.requirement: An estate at will may be determined by either party by three months' written notice, or, if rent is payable at periods of less than three months, by written notice equal to the interval between payment days or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.key_value: 3 months, or interval between payment days or 30 days, whichever is longer
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

rules.title: Inclusion of Offer for New Tenancy in Termination Notice
rules.requirement: A written notice to determine an estate at will may include an offer to establish a new tenancy for the same premises on different terms, and the inclusion of such an offer does not affect the validity of the notice.
rules.quoted_span: Such written notice may include an offer to establish a new tenancy for the same premises on terms different from that of the tenancy being terminated and the validity of such written notice shall not be affected by the inclusion of such offer.

rules.title: Fourteen Days' Notice to Quit for Nonpayment
rules.requirement: A landlord may determine an estate at will for a tenant's neglect or refusal to pay rent due by giving the tenant fourteen days' written notice to quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies in case of neglect or refusal to pay rent due from a tenant at will.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;

rules.title: Right to Cure Nonpayment Within Ten Days
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will is not determined if a tenant who has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months pays or tenders the full amount of rent due within ten days after receiving the notice to quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding receipt of the notice.
rules.quoted_span: provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: Mandatory Notification Language in Nonpayment Notice
rules.requirement: Every notice determining an estate at will for nonpayment of rent must include verbatim statutory notification informing the tenant of the right to cure within ten days if no notice to quit for nonpayment was received within the prior twelve months.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to every notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent.
rules.quoted_span: Every notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall contain the following notification to the tenant: ''If you have not received a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent within the last twelve months, you have a right to prevent termination of your tenancy by paying or tendering to your landlord, your landlord's attorney or the person to whom you customarily pay your rent the full amount of rent due within ten days after your receipt of this notice.''

rules.title: Extension of Cure Period for Omission of Required Notification
rules.requirement: If a nonpayment notice fails to include the mandatory notification, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in an action to recover possession, though the failure to include the notification does not otherwise affect the validity of the notice.
rules.key_value: extended to the day the answer is due
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent fails to contain the required notification.
rules.quoted_span: If any notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall fail to contain such notification, the time within which the tenant receiving the notice would be entitled to pay or tender rent pursuant to this section shall be extended to the day the answer is due in any action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises. Failure to include such notice shall not otherwise affect the validity of the said notice.

rules.title: Continuance and Reinstatement for Government Subsidy Delay
rules.requirement: If nonpayment was caused by a government delay or failure in delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check, or voucher, the court in a possession action must continue the hearing for at least seven days to notify the agency and must treat the tenancy as not terminated if rent, interest, and court costs are tendered within that time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when neglect or refusal to pay rent was caused by government delay or failure in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check, or voucher (other than salary) to the tenant or landlord.
rules.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any action for possession shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.

rules.title: Maximum payments required at commencement of tenancy
rules.requirement: At or prior to the commencement of tenancy, a lessor or agent cannot require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay any amount exceeding first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a security deposit equal to first month's rent (or a regulated optional fee in lieu of a security deposit up to one month's rent), and key and lock purchase and installation costs.
rules.key_value: First month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit equal to 1 month's rent, and key and lock cost
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);  provided, however, that the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit;  provided further, that any such regulations shall:  (A) require the lessor to utilize a fee collected to waive a security deposit to cover for unpaid rent or unit damage that applies to the tenant's lease;  (B) require that a fee so collected be:  (I) entirely or partially non-refundable;  provided, however, that the lessor shall disclose that the fee is non-refundable in the lease;  provided further, that the tenant shall agree to the fee and acknowledge that the tenant understand that it is entirely or partially non-refundable, as the case may be, in writing;  and (II) a recurring monthly fee, or payable upon any schedule and in an amount that the lessor and tenant agree upon, as authorized by the executive office;  (C) limit the total sum of the fee or recurring payments, regardless of the duration of the lease and any extensions thereto, to an amount not to exceed 1 month's rent;  (D) require that the fee be made optional for both the tenant and the lessor and that the tenant be permitted to choose to pay a full security deposit rather than the fee;  (E) require a lessor who offers such a fee in lieu of security deposit:  (I) to offer the option of a fee in lieu of a security deposit to every prospective tenant whose application for occupancy has been approved, regardless of income, race, gender, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, immigration status, size of household or credit score;  and (II) not to consider such factors and categories when setting the amount of the fee;  and (F) allow a tenant who agrees to pay a fee to waive a security deposit to opt-out of the obligation to pay such fee if such tenant pays the security deposit that would otherwise be in effect for the tenant's apartment on the day the tenant chooses to opt-out of such fee;  provided further, that the sum of fees paid to waive a security deposit and the payment of the security deposit shall not exceed, in total, the amount of 1 month's rent;  and provided further, that the executive office shall consult with the office of the attorney general prior to promulgating regulations authorizing a fee in lieu of a security deposit under this section;  and,
(iv) the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.

rules.title: Prohibition on subsequent demand for advance rent or excess security deposit
rules.requirement: A lessor or successor in interest cannot demand advance rent exceeding the current month's rent or a security deposit exceeding the allowable statutory amount at any time after tenancy commencement.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (d) No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.  The payment in advance for occupancy pursuant to this section shall be binding upon all successors in interest.

rules.title: Tenant ownership, non-commingling, and creditor protection of security deposit
rules.requirement: A security deposit remains the tenant's property, must not be commingled with the lessor's assets, and is shielded from claims by any creditor of the lessor or successor in interest, including foreclosing mortgagees and bankruptcy trustees.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (e) A security deposit shall continue to be the property of the tenant making such deposit, shall not be commingled with the assets of the lessor, and shall not be subject to the claims of any creditor of the lessor or of the lessor's successor in interest, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy;  provided, however, that the tenant shall be entitled to only such interest as is provided for in subsection (3)(b).

rules.title: Receipt for advance last month's rent
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent receiving advance last month's rent at or prior to commencement must provide a written receipt at payment stating the amount, date received, intended application, recipient's name (and lessor's name if received by an agent), premises description, statement of interest entitlement at 5% per year or the bank rate received, and instruction to provide a forwarding address upon termination.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (2)(a) Any lessor or his agent who receives, at or prior to the commencement of a tenancy, rent in advance for the last month of the tenancy from a tenant or prospective tenant shall give to such tenant or prospective tenant at the time of such advance payment a receipt indicating the amount of such rent, the date on which it was received, its intended application as rent for the last month of the tenancy, the name of the person receiving it and, in the case of an agent, the name of the lessor for whom the rent is received, and a description of the rented or leased premises, and a statement indicating that the tenant is entitled to interest on said rent payment at the rate of five per cent per year or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable in accordance with the provisions of this clause, and a statement indicating that the tenant should provide the lessor with a forwarding address at the termination of the tenancy indicating where such interest may be given or sent.

rules.title: Interest and annual statement for advance last month's rent
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent holding advance last month's rent must pay annual interest starting from the first day of tenancy at 5% per year (or the lesser bank rate received) and furnish an annual statement and payment or deduction notification; if not received within thirty days from the end of each tenancy year, the tenant may deduct the interest due from the next rental payment. Accrued interest must be paid within thirty days if the tenancy terminates before the anniversary date.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser amount received from bank
rules.exemptions: Interest shall not accrue for the last month for which rent was paid in advance.; Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor or his agent who receives said rent in advance for the last month of tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held.  Such interest shall be paid over to the tenant each year as provided in this clause;  provided, however, that in the event that the tenancy is terminated before the anniversary date of such tenancy, the tenant shall receive all accrued interest within thirty days of such termination.  Interest shall not accrue for the last month for which rent was paid in advance.  At the end of each year of tenancy, such lessor shall give or send to the tenant from whom rent in advance was collected a statement which shall indicate the amount payable by such lessor to the tenant.  The lessor shall at the same time give or send to such tenant the interest which is due or shall notify the tenant that he may deduct the interest from the next rental payment of such tenant.  If, after thirty days from the end of each year of the tenancy, the tenant has not received said interest due or said notice to deduct the interest from the next rental payment, the tenant may deduct from his next rent payment the interest due.

rules.title: Treble damages for failure to pay interest on last month's rent upon termination
rules.requirement: If a lessor fails to pay accrued interest on advance last month's rent within thirty days after tenancy termination, the tenant shall be awarded three times the amount of interest due, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Three times the amount of interest due
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor fails to pay any interest to which the tenant is then entitled within thirty days after the termination of the tenancy, the tenant upon proof of the same in an action against the lessor shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of interest to which the tenant is entitled, together with court costs and reasonable attorneys fees.

rules.title: Security deposit receipt upon payment
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent receiving a security deposit must provide a signed receipt at the time of receipt stating the deposit amount, date received, recipient's name (and lessor's name if received by an agent), and a description of the leased or rented premises.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (b) Any lessor or his agent who receives a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall give said tenant or prospective tenant at the time of receiving such security deposit a receipt indicating the amount of such security deposit, the name of the person receiving it and, in the case of an agent, the name of the lessor for whom such security deposit is received, the date on which it is received, and a description of the premises leased or rented.  Said receipt shall be signed by the person receiving the security deposit.

rules.title: Statement of condition of premises
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent accepting a security deposit must furnish upon receipt or within ten days after tenancy commencement (whichever is later) a signed written statement listing existing damage and certified or adjudicated sanitary/building code violations with a mandatory twelve-point bold notice; if the tenant returns a separate list of damages within fifteen days, the lessor must return a copy within fifteen days with signed agreement or a clear statement of disagreement.
rules.key_value: Within 10 days after commencement or upon receipt, whichever is later
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(c) Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.  Such written statement shall also contain a comprehensive listing of any damage then existing in the premises, including, but not limited to, any violations of the state sanitary or state building codes certified by a local board of health or building official or adjudicated by a court and then existing in the premises.  Such statement shall be signed by the lessor or his agent and contain the following notice in twelve-point bold-face type at the top of the first page thereof:
"This is a statement of the condition of the premises you have leased or rented.  You should read it carefully in order to see if it is correct.  If it is correct you must sign it.  This will show that you agree that the list is correct and complete.  If it is not correct, you must attach a separate signed list of any damage which you believe exists in the premises.  This statement must be returned to the lessor or his agent within fifteen days after you receive this list or within fifteen days after you move in, whichever is later.  If you do not return this list, within the specified time period, a court may later view your failure to return the list as your agreement that the list is complete and correct in any suit which you may bring to recover the security deposit.''
If the tenant submits to the lessor or his agent a separate list of damages, the lessor or his agent shall, within fifteen days of receiving said separate list, return a copy of said list to the tenant with either such lessor's signed agreement with the content thereof or a clear statement of disagreement attached.

rules.title: Security deposit record keeping, inspection, and remedy
rules.requirement: A lessor accepting security deposits must maintain records containing damage descriptions, termination dates, repair costs, receipts, and copies of condition statements and receipts for two years following tenancy termination; records must be made available for tenant inspection during business hours, and wrongful failure to make them available entitles the tenant to immediate return of the security deposit plus accrued interest.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(d) Every lessor who accepts a security deposit shall maintain a record of all such security deposits received which contains the following information:--
(i) a detailed description of any damage done to each of the dwelling units or premises for which a security deposit has been accepted, returned to any tenant thereof or for which the lessor has brought suit against any tenant;
(ii) the date upon which the occupancy of the tenant or tenants charged with such damage was terminated;  and
(iii) whether repairs were performed to remedy such damage, the dates of said repairs, the cost thereof, and receipts therefor.
Said record shall also include copies of any receipt or statement of condition given to a tenant or prospective tenant as required by this section.
Said record shall be available for inspection upon request of a tenant or prospective tenant during normal business hours in the office of the lessor or his agent.  Upon a wrongful failure by the lessor or his agent to make such record available for inspection by a tenant or prospective tenant, said tenant or prospective tenant shall be entitled to the immediate return of any amount paid in the form of a security deposit together with any interest which has accrued thereon.
The lessor or his agent shall maintain said record for each dwelling unit or premises for which a security deposit was accepted for a period of two years from the date of termination of the tenancy or occupancy upon which the security deposit was conditioned.

rules.title: Holding security deposit in separate bank account, bank receipt, and remedy
rules.requirement: A security deposit must be held in a separate, interest-bearing bank account located in Massachusetts beyond the reach of the lessor's creditors; the lessor must provide the tenant a receipt within thirty days of deposit receipt stating the bank's name, location, amount, and account number, and failure to comply entitles the tenant to immediate return of the deposit.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (3) (a) Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.  A receipt shall be given to the tenant within thirty days after such deposit is received by the lessor which receipt shall indicate the name and location of the bank in which the security deposit has been deposited and the amount and account number of said deposit.  Failure to comply with this paragraph shall entitle the tenant to immediate return of the security deposit.

rules.title: Annual interest payment and statement for security deposit
rules.requirement: A lessor holding a security deposit for one year or longer must pay interest from the first day of tenancy at 5% per year (or the lesser bank rate received) and provide an annual statement and payment or deduction notification; if not received within thirty days from the end of each tenancy year, the tenant may deduct the interest from the next rental payment. If terminated before the anniversary date, accrued interest must be paid within thirty days.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser amount received from bank
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a lessor holding a security deposit for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (b) A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.  Such interest shall be paid over to the tenant each year as provided in this clause, provided, however, that in the event that the tenancy is terminated before the anniversary date of the tenancy, the tenant shall receive all accrued interest within thirty days of such termination.  Such interest shall be beyond the claims of such lessor, except as provided for in this section.  At the end of each year of a tenancy, such lessor shall give or send to the tenant from whom a security deposit has been received a statement which shall indicate the name and address of the bank in which the security deposit has been placed, the amount of the deposit, the account number, and the amount of interest payable by such lessor to the tenant.  The lessor shall at the same time give or send to each such tenant the interest which is due or shall include with the statement required by this clause a notification that the tenant may deduct the interest from the tenant's next rental payment.  If, after thirty days from the end of each year of the tenancy, the tenant has not received such notice or payment, the tenant may deduct from his next rent payment the interest due.

rules.title: Return of security deposit, permitted deductions, and itemized damage list
rules.requirement: A lessor must return the security deposit or balance within thirty days after termination of occupancy, minus permitted deductions solely for unpaid rent/water, tax escalation, or reasonable damage repair beyond wear and tear; damage deductions require providing within thirty days an itemized list sworn under pains and penalties of perjury and written cost evidence, and no deduction may be made for pre-existing damages unless repaired and renewed.
rules.key_value: Within 30 days after termination of occupancy
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(4) The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following:
(i) any unpaid rent or water charges which have not been validly withheld or deducted pursuant to any general or special law
(ii) any unpaid increase in real estate taxes which the tenant is obligated to pay pursuant to a tax escalation clause which conforms to the requirements of section fifteen C;  and
(iii) a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant or any person under the tenant's control or on the premises with the tenant's consent, reasonable wear and tear excluded.  In the case of such damage, the lessor shall provide to the tenant within such thirty days an itemized list of damages, sworn to by the lessor or his agent under pains and penalties of perjury, itemizing in precise detail the nature of the damage and of the repairs necessary to correct such damage, and written evidence, such as estimates, bills, invoices or receipts, indicating the actual or estimated cost thereof.  No amount shall be deducted from the security deposit for any damage to the dwelling unit which was listed in the separate written statement of the present condition of the premises which was required to be given to the tenant prior to the execution of the lease or creation of the tenancy pursuant to clause (c) of subsection (2) or any damages listed in any separate list submitted by the tenant and signed by the lessor or his agent pursuant to said clause (c), unless the lessor subsequently repaired or caused to be repaired said damage and can prove that the renewed damage was unrelated to the prior damage and was caused by the tenant or by any person under the tenant's control or on the premises with the tenant's consent.  Nothing in this section shall limit the right of a landlord to recover from a tenant, who wilfully or maliciously destroys or damages the real or personal property of said landlord, to the forfeiture of a security deposit, when the cost of repairing or replacing such property exceeds the amount of such security deposit.
No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section.

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor in interest
rules.requirement: Upon transferring interest in a dwelling unit, a lessor must transfer the security deposit and accrued interest to the successor in interest, who must provide written notice to the tenant within 45 days; the transferor remains liable until notice and transfer or return occur, and a successor assumes liability even if the prior lessor fails to transfer the funds (with an exception for municipalities under chapter 60 and chartered financial institutions).
rules.exemptions: The granting of a mortgage is not deemed a transfer of interest. The liability assumption on successors does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty or a foreclosing/possessing mortgagee that is a chartered financial institution.; Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(5) Whenever a lessor who receives a security deposit transfers his interest in the dwelling unit for which the security deposit is held, whether by sale, assignment, death, appointment of a receiver or trustee in bankruptcy, or otherwise, the lessor shall transfer such security deposit together with any interest which has accrued thereon for the benefit of the tenant who made such security deposit to his successor in interest, and said successor in interest shall be liable for the retention and return of said security deposit in accordance with the provisions of this section from the date upon which said transfer is made;  provided however, that the granting of a mortgage on such premises shall not be a transfer of interest.  The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such security deposit that such security deposit was transferred to him and that he is holding said security deposit.  Such notice shall also contain the lessor's name, business address, and business telephone number, and the name, business address, and business telephone number of his agent, if any.  Said notice shall be in writing.
Upon such transfer, the lessor or his agent shall continue to be liable with respect to the provisions of this section until:
(a) there has been a transfer of the amount of the security deposit so held to the lessor's successor in interest and the tenant has been notified in writing of the transfer and of the successor in interest's name, business address, and business telephone number;
(b) there has been compliance with this clause by the successor in interest;  or
(c) the security deposit has been returned to the tenant.
In the event that the lessor fails to transfer said security deposit to his successor in interest as required by this subsection the successor in interest shall, without regard to the nature of the transfer, assume liability for payment of the security deposit to the tenant in accordance with the provisions of this section;  provided, however, that if the tenant still occupies the dwelling unit for which the security deposit was given, said successor in interest may satisfy such obligation by granting the tenant free use and occupancy of the dwelling unit for a period of time equivalent to that period of time for which the dwelling unit could be leased or occupied if the security deposit were deemed to be rent.  The liability imposed by this paragraph shall not apply to a city or town which acquires title to property pursuant to chapter sixty or to a foreclosing mortgagee or a mortgagee in possession which is a financial institution chartered by the commonwealth or the United States.  The term "rent'', as used in the preceding sentence, shall mean the periodic sum paid by the tenant for the use and occupation of the dwelling unit in accordance with the terms of his lease or other rental agreement.

rules.title: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit or counterclaim for damages
rules.requirement: A lessor forfeits the right to retain any portion of a security deposit or counterclaim for property damage if the lessor fails to deposit funds in a compliant bank account, fails to furnish an itemized damage list within thirty days, attempts to enforce conflicting lease terms or obtain waivers, fails to transfer the deposit to a successor, or fails to return the deposit balance with interest within thirty days after termination.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]

rules.title: Treble damages, interest, costs, and attorney's fees for deposit violations
rules.requirement: If a lessor or agent fails to deposit funds into a separate account, fails to transfer the deposit to a successor, or fails to return the deposit or balance due within thirty days after termination, the tenant shall be awarded damages equal to three times the amount of the deposit or balance, plus 5% interest from the due date, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Three times the security deposit or balance due plus 5% interest
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]

rules.title: Transfer of advance last month's rent to successor in interest
rules.requirement: Upon transferring interest in a dwelling unit, a lessor must credit advance last month's rent and accrued interest to the successor, and the successor must provide written notice to the tenant within 45 days; the transferor remains liable until proper notice and credit or payment occur, and a successor assumes liability even if the prior lessor fails to credit the advance (with an exception for municipalities under chapter 60 and chartered financial institutions).
rules.exemptions: The granting of a mortgage is not deemed a transfer of interest. The liability assumption on successors does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty or a foreclosing/possessing mortgagee that is a chartered financial institution.; Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
(7A) Whenever a lessor who receives rent in advance for the last month of tenancy transfers his interest in the dwelling unit for which the rental advance was received, whether by sale, assignment, death, appointment of a receiver or trustee in bankruptcy, or otherwise, the lessor shall credit an amount equal to such rental advance together with any interest which has accrued thereon for the benefit of the tenant who made such rental advance, to the successor in interest of such lessor, and said successor in interest shall be liable for crediting the tenant with such rental advance, and for paying all interest accrued thereon in accordance with the provisions of this section from the date upon which said transfer is made;  provided, however, that the granting of a mortgage on such premises shall not be deemed a transfer of interest.  The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such rental advance that such rental advance was so credited, and that such successor has assumed responsibility therefor pursuant to the foregoing provision.  Such notice shall also contain the lessor's name, business address, and business telephone number, and the name, business address, and business telephone number of his agent, if any.  Said notice shall be in writing.
Upon such transfer, the lessor or his agent shall continue to be liable with respect to the provisions of this section until:--(a) there has been a credit of the amount of the rental advance so held to the lessor's successor in interest and the tenant has been notified in writing of the transfer and of the successor in interest's name, business address, and business telephone number;  (b) there has been compliance with this clause by the successor in interest;  or (c) the rental advance has been credited to the tenant and all accrued interest has been paid thereon.
In the event that the lessor fails to credit said rental advance to his successor in interest as required by this subsection, the successor in interest shall, without regard to the nature of the transfer, assume liability for crediting of the rental advance, and payment of all interest thereon to the tenant in accordance with the provisions of this section;  provided, however, that if the tenant still occupies the dwelling unit for which the rental advance was given, said successor in interest may satisfy such obligation by granting the tenant free use and occupancy of the dwelling unit for a period of time equivalent to the period of time covered by the rental advance.  The liability imposed by this subsection shall not apply to a city or town which acquires title to property pursuant to chapter sixty or to a foreclosing mortgagee or a mortgagee in possession which is a financial institution chartered by the commonwealth or by the United States.

rules.title: Anti-waiver and invalidity of conflicting lease provisions
rules.requirement: Any lease provision conflicting with Section 15B and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of Section 15B is void, unenforceable, and against public policy.
rules.exemptions: Section 15B does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy, or tenancy of 100 days or less in duration that is for a vacation or recreational purpose. [M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(9); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span: (8) Any provision of a lease which conflicts with any provision of this section and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Broker fee payment restriction
rules.requirement: Any broker fee must only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant, who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent - Required accompanying form and disclosures
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent served by a landlord on a residential tenant must be accompanied by a form documenting any tenant repayment agreements, providing information on rental assistance programs, trial court summary process rules/orders, and eviction restrictions, and prominently displaying the mandatory notice that a notice to quit is not an eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter.
rules.quoted_span:
Section 31. (a) A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to: (i) documentation of any agreements between the tenant and landlord for the tenant to repay the landlord for nonpayment of rent; and (ii) information on: (1) rental assistance programs including, but not limited to, the residential assistance for families in transition program; (2) applicable trial court rules, standing orders or emergency administrative orders pertaining to actions for summary process; and (3) any relevant federal or state legal restrictions on residential evictions. The form shall also prominently display the following statement:
''THIS NOTICE TO QUIT IS NOT AN EVICTION. YOU DO NOT NEED TO IMMEDIATELY LEAVE YOUR UNIT. YOU ARE ENTITLED TO A LEGAL PROCEEDING IN WHICH YOU CAN DEFEND AGAINST THE EVICTION. ONLY A COURT ORDER CAN FORCE YOU TO LEAVE YOUR UNIT.''

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent - Proof of form delivery required for court filing
rules.requirement: In an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, no court having jurisdiction over summary process may accept for filing a writ, summons, or complaint without proof of delivery of the required form.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit in actions for summary process pursuant to chapter 239.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section.

rules.title: Housing Application Criminal Record Inquiries Prohibited Prior to Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application containing inquiries regarding criminal records prior to providing a conditional offer. A housing provider may only inquire about convictions for methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.

rules.title: Pre-Offer Criminal Record Inquiries Prohibited
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

rules.title: Written Disclosures Required Prior to Accepting Application Fee
rules.requirement: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review and consideration of criminal history, and that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]

rules.title: Nondiscriminatory Application of Application Standards
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall apply the statutory application process standards to each applicant in a nondiscriminatory manner.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]

rules.title: Prohibited Criminal Records in Applicant Evaluation
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not evaluate an applicant, either before or after a conditional offer, based on arrests or charges not resulting in conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile delinquency adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]

rules.title: Permissible Criminal Records After Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: After issuing a conditional offer, a housing provider may only consider convictions for specified major offenses or lifetime sex offender registration, or indictable offenses within defined time limits: first degree within six years, second or third degree within four years, and fourth degree within one year.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
After the issuance of a conditional offer to an
applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the
applicant’s history that:
(1)   resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated
sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in
violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a

(3)   is for an indictable offense of the second or
third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison
sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding
the issuance of the conditional offer; or
(4)   is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the
conditional offer.

rules.title: Standard for Withdrawing Conditional Offer Based on Criminal Record
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if it determines by a preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a

provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is

rules.title: Written Notice and Opportunity to Appeal Withdrawal
rules.requirement: Upon withdrawing a conditional offer, a housing provider must provide the applicant with written notice stating specific reasons for the withdrawal and offering an opportunity to appeal by submitting evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]
rules.quoted_span:
If a housing provider withdraws a conditional
offer, the housing provider shall provide the applicant with written

providing evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies within
the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.

rules.title: Individualized Assessment Factors Before Withdrawal
rules.requirement: The housing provider must perform an individualized assessment considering the offense's nature and severity, applicant's age at occurrence, time elapsed, rehabilitation evidence, safety risks if reoccurring, and whether the offense occurred on or was connected to rented property.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit. [P.L. 2021, c.110, § 3 (C.46:8-54)]

of the criminal offense;

rules.requirement: An applicant may request within 30 days of withdrawal notice a copy of all information relied upon by the housing provider, which the housing provider must provide free of charge within 10 days of receiving the request.

rules.requirement: No person shall interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of any right protected under this act, and any retaliatory action taken against a person for filing a complaint shall be enforced as a separate violation.

rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] An owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the rent cap by providing evidence that an increase above the annual allowance is necessary for a fair and reasonable return. rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Tenancy Termination
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] An owner cannot terminate a tenancy after 30 days without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies after 30 days of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: The Just Cause Eviction Ordinance does not apply to certain property types, including housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters. [Just Cause Eviction Ordinance]
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: At-Fault Just Cause Grounds
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] At-fault grounds for eviction include default in rent payment, breach of a material lease term, committing a nuisance, criminal activity, and other specified actions.
rules.exemptions: The Just Cause Eviction Ordinance does not apply to certain property types, including housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters. [Just Cause Eviction Ordinance]
rules.quoted_span: “Just cause” includes certain at-fault causes such as default in payment of rent, breach of a material term of the lease, committing a nuisance, criminal activity, and other actions.

rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause Grounds
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] No-fault grounds for eviction include owner occupancy, removal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.
rules.exemptions: The Just Cause Eviction Ordinance does not apply to certain property types, including housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters. [Just Cause Eviction Ordinance]
rules.quoted_span: “Just cause” also includes certain no-fault causes such as the intent of the owner to occupy the property, removal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.

rules.title: Notice of Violation and Opportunity to Cure
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause, an owner must first provide notice of the violation and give the tenant a time period to fix the violation.
rules.exemptions: The Just Cause Eviction Ordinance does not apply to certain property types, including housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters. [Just Cause Eviction Ordinance]
rules.quoted_span: Before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause, the owner shall first give notice of the violation with a time period for the tenant to fix the violation(s).
